concept.name: Secondhand Fit
concept.oneLiner: Try-on for resale listings, where the only photo is a wrinkled flat-lay on someone's bedroom floor.
concept.targetUser: Buyers on peer-to-peer resale marketplaces, and the individual sellers listing one-of-one items with phone photos.
concept.problem: Resale is the fastest-growing part of apparel commerce and the hardest to shop: every item is unique, non-returnable in practice, and photographed as a flat-lay on a bed or hanging on a door. Buyers cannot picture it on themselves, so they either skip the item or buy and resell again. Sellers have no studio and no model, and marketplace try-on tools assume clean e-commerce product imagery that resale listings never have.
concept.solution: Secondhand Fit is a listing-side and buyer-side layer for resale. On the seller side, a guided capture flow turns a phone flat-lay into a VTO-ready garment image: the app checks flatness, background separation and garment framing, auto-crops, and reports a 'try-on readiness' grade with specific retake instructions before the listing goes live. On the buyer side, one consented selfie renders the item through YouCam Apparel VTO, with a readiness badge that tells the buyer how much to trust the render given the source photo quality. Every render carries a preview-only label and a hard exclusion on fit, sizing and condition claims.
concept.coreWorkflow: Seller uploads phone photo → readiness checks (flatness, background, framing, occlusion) with concrete retake prompts → accepted image normalised and stored with a readiness grade → listing publishes with a 'try-on ready' badge → buyer taps try-on, consents, uploads a selfie → server calls YouCam Apparel VTO with the normalised garment and the buyer photo → render returns with the readiness badge and honest label → buyer saves the render to their watchlist; seller sees how many try-ons their listing generated.
concept.sponsorTechnology: YouCam Apparel Virtual Try-On as the render engine, with the pre-processing pipeline built specifically to satisfy its input constraints.
